dialogue.text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. When did your chest pain and shortness of breath begin, and have you noticed any fever or chills?

The chest pain and the shortness of breath started about a week ago, right around the time I started coughing up this thick, nasty phlegm. I've definitely been feeling feverish and just generally worn out lately. It's been pretty rough ever since I stopped taking that medicine for the flu I had.
That sounds very difficult to manage. Could you tell me what color the phlegm is, and does your chest pain feel worse when you take a deep breath or cough?
The phlegm is a thick, yellowish-green color. My chest hurts a lot more whenever I try to take a deep breath or have a coughing fit.
I'd like to perform a physical exam to listen to your lungs. Have you ever smoked, or do you have any long-term health conditions like asthma or COPD? REQUEST TEST: Physical_Exam

RESULTS: Temperature: 38.7°C (101.7°F), Blood Pressure: 120/60 mm Hg, Heart Rate: 70 bpm, Respiratory Rate: 22 breaths/min, SO2: 80%. Inspection: No cyanosis or use of accessory respiratory muscles. Auscultation: Decreased breath sounds at the left base, crackles. Percussion: Dullness to percussion over the left lower lung fields. Palpation: No significant findings.
Your oxygen level is dangerously low at 80 percent, which is a medical emergency. You need immediate medical attention and should go to the emergency room right now. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-
RESULTS: Alveolar infiltrates in the left base with air bronchograms
Your oxygen levels are critically low at 80%, so please call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room immediately. Based on your symptoms and the X-ray showing alveolar infiltrates

Wait, are you saying this is an emergency? I knew I felt short of breath, but I didn't realize it was that serious. I'll head to the hospital right away—I should have finished those flu meds like I was told.

Yes, this is a serious medical emergency and you need to be seen immediately. Please go to the emergency room now or call 911.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Pneumonia
